notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for mission-critical inference (customer-facing chat + rerank for product search). Primary drivers: strict latency SLOs for real-time chat, predictable monthly spend, and strong tenant isolation for multi-tenant retail services. They are risk-averse around noisy-neighbor effects and want hard guarantees for priority lanes.

Key requirements (explicit):
- Throughput guarantees: sustain 400 concurrent chat sessions at ~50 tokens/sec average each (target sustained throughput ~20k tokens/sec), with ability to burst to 1k concurrent during peak (Black Friday traffic).
- Latency SLOs: 95p tail < 250ms for short interactive chat (<= 256 output tokens), P99 < 400ms during steady state for chat. For reranking endpoints, p95 < 120ms for top-10 rerank jobs.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial commit: equivalent of 8x A100-80GB class GPUs (mix of inference-optimized instances) with ability to add 4 GPUs month-to-month. Wants pricing for 12-month reserved vs 3-month trial.
- SLA asks: 99.95% uptime, latency SLO credits for p95 breaches, scheduled maintenance windows (48-72h notice), and an escalation path with named SREs.
- Traffic shaping & priority lanes: MUST have per-route min/max capacity and priority queueing. Requirements:
  * Per-route quotas (tokens/sec + requests/sec) with hard caps and soft throttling.
  * Priority lanes to isolate critical routes (search/rerank/chat-auth) from lower-priority experimental workloads.
  * Noisy-neighbor controls: automatic backpressure, token-weighted fair queuing, and preemption rules for low-priority batches.
  * Tenant isolation: resource reservations at tenant or route level (GPU reservations or guaranteed share), and per-tenant metrics (GPU util, queue depth, latency histograms).
  * Overflow policy: transparent fallback to Redwood-hosted pool or queue with clear SLAs for overflow traffic.

- Acceptance: p95 chat latency < 300ms under 10% CPU/GPU contention added, per-route quotas enforceable (measured by token/sec limits), and retention of audit logs for all requests.
